item.text: I’m reviewing what’s still awkward in the current design before changing more code. The biggest remaining issue is the fixed-capacity array and compatibility-shaped API, so I’m targeting a more idiomatic heap core rather than another round of surface cleanup.

I’m going to refactor toward a dynamically resizing heap with standard queue-style operations, then preserve the old method names as thin wrappers so existing callers still work. After that I’ll broaden the tests around resizing and bulk construction.

I’m replacing the fixed-capacity backing array with a growable one, adding bulk heap construction, and tightening the public surface around snapshots and removal order. The legacy method names will stay, but they’ll sit on top of the newer core paths.

I’m updating the tests to match the new heap shape: growth instead of hard capacity failure, heapify-from-array, snapshot copying, and clear semantics. That should give us better regression coverage than the earlier demo-style checks.
The refactor is written. I’m compiling and running the full test harness now to validate the new growth and heapify paths, since those are the most likely places for subtle regressions.

Refactored the heap into a more idiomatic, reusable structure in [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:4). The main change is that the backing array now grows automatically via [ensureCapacity](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:155), so inserts no longer depend on a fixed one-time capacity. I also added a default constructor, a bulk-construction path that heapifies an input array in linear time, `clear`, and a defensive `toArray` snapshot.

The mutation paths are a bit cleaner now as well. `removeMin` delegates through [removeAt](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:67), stale slots are cleared on removal, and the legacy method names still map to the newer queue-style core API. One behavior change to note: `insertKey` now succeeds by growing the heap instead of returning `false` when the initial capacity is exhausted.

I expanded the test harness in [MinHeapTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeapTest.java:4) to cover dynamic growth, bulk heapify construction, `clear`, defensive snapshots, and removal ordering helpers, while keeping the original example flow as a compatibility check.

Verification: `javac MinHeap.java MinHeapTest.java && java MinHeapTest` passed.
